title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Carduus root has distinct winter-food and topical deodorant uses
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Lonitzer's complete 1551 Carduus/Scolymus entry explicitly names roots as a salted/peppered winter second course and then names radix as an external application for armpit/body odor. Preserve the same plant-part identity across two distinct routes and outcomes, without turning 'root' into a free-standing part label. The source's separate decocted-food urine claim is not forcibly bound to the root.

source.url: retained local primary transcription; no external page accessed
source.span: Lonitzer, Kreuterbuch (1551), complete Carduus entry, F_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md lines 33–70; internal and external uses at lines 54–57; source layer CAMENA typed edition, not a fully corrected diplomatic transcription
source.observed_content: The account says roots are eaten with salt and pepper as a winter second course, and separately says an applied root corrects armpit and whole-body odor. The next clause assigns abundant foul-smelling urine to a decoction in foods; its grammatical part-owner is not fixed here.
source.layer: Historical primary-text content in retained typed-edition/transcription layer; no new manuscript collation or target access

potential_admitted_target: None asserted; root must independently identify any permitted complete target unit before review.

design.mechanism: Bind a named plant root across two locally distinct use frames: internal culinary consumption with winter timing and salt/pepper, then external application with armpit/body-odor outcome. The part persists while route, operation and bodily consequence change. Keep the subsequent decocted-food/urine claim out of this root-specific chain unless its source syntax is independently resolved.
design.unit: Complete Lonitzer Carduus account, including the internal and external VIRES sections, within F_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md; no Voynich unit was inspected.
design.observable_consequence: A later root-owned whole-unit reading would need to carry one part identity into two different operation/route contexts and preserve the external body-region effect; a lone part label, one generic preparation, or adjacency without a repeated owned part and distinct outcome would not meet the source-specific model. No assertion is made that a target has this structure.
design.scope: Source-only raw proposal; unreviewed, unselected, untested, and no target glosses

execution_requirements: Before selection, root must identify a permitted complete unit and own any target inspection.
Keep lexical part identity, food route, topical route, season, applied body region and result as separately bound roles.
Treat the urine claim as a bounded ambiguity unless its grammatical owner is securely fixed in the source edition.
Retain a one-use/part-label rival; do not add free target glosses or use a guessed plant identity.
assumptions_and_limits: The complete entry distinguishes cultivated spiny and spineless Carduus forms and also discusses Scolymon/wild thistle; these taxa must not be silently collapsed into a modern species.
This is a CAMENA typed edition with retained source HTML, not a fully corrected diplomatic manuscript transcription.
Historical medicinal claims are not clinical evidence. The design asserts no target availability, fit, or word meaning.

IDEA000797 concerns Atractylis ingestion versus holding/release; IDEA000782 is a broader portion-constructor family. This proposal concerns the same named Carduus root used in two specific culinary/topical frames, but remains subject to duplicate review.
